args.code:
tbl = bytes.fromhex('24 e4 b5 72 07 86 1d bc 4c c4 5e c1 9a 16 b7 59 cc 7a e7 b8 70 48 88 db 66')
assert len(tbl)==25
s=0x62
inp=[]
for b in tbl:
    x=b ^ s
    inp.append(x)
    s=(s + x) & 0xff
print('input bytes:', inp)
print('as hex:', bytes(inp).hex())
print('as latin1:', bytes(inp))
try:
    print('as ascii:', bytes(inp).decode('ascii'))
except Exception as e:
    print('ascii decode fails', e)
print('printables:', ''.join(chr(c) if 32<=c<127 else '.' for c in inp))

args.text: Disassembly shows main (0x4010b0) checks argv[1]. It first computes a 64-bit inequality from len via multiplications; if the computed rdx is >= 0x1111111111111110 it falls into direct strcmp against embedded string at 0x404030 (FLAG{basalt_ferrite_7556}). Otherwise (for typical lengths) it requires length==0x19 (25) and then runs a rolling check: start edx=0x62, for i=0..24: ecx=argv1[i]; require (edx ^ ecx) == table[i] where table is 25 bytes at 0x402040; then edx += ecx. Inverting this yields unique input bytes producing table: ASCII 'FLAG{quartz_granite_6483}'.

retrieved_cards.title: Flag-shaped string with no reference from the accept path
retrieved_cards.applicability_signal: A printable, delimiter-wrapped, flag-like string appears in a static string dump or .rodata, but no code path from the comparison/accept logic references it.
retrieved_cards.mechanism: Visibility of data is conflated with semantic relevance; a string may exist for logging or as a plant and never be compared against the input.
retrieved_cards.validation_note: Establish a cross-reference from the comparison/accept logic to the string, and follow that comparison's result to the branch that decides acceptance; appearing in a string dump is not a reference.
retrieved_cards.misleading_interpretation: The visible flag-shaped string is the answer and can be submitted directly.
retrieved_cards.better_interpretation: A visible string is a candidate at most; relevance is established by a reference from the comparison whose outcome selects the accepting branch, not by visibility.
not_applicable_when: the string is referenced from the accept/comparison path
the string is the operand of the comparison that the accepting branch consumes
the target is known not to gate on a static string (e.g. a purely computed check)
misfire_risks: in trivial tasks the flag genuinely is a plain static string; look for the xref that confirms it rather than discarding the candidate outright
minimum_evidence_before_use: a flag-shaped string was located in a static dump
no reference from the accept path to that string has been established yet

provenance.authoring_note: Abstract decoy-string pattern; no task-specific constants, flags, functions, or addresses.

retrieved_cards.title: Inline data or junk bytes can be rendered as instructions
retrieved_cards.applicability_signal: Bytes that are actually data (jump tables, constants, padding) or deliberate junk are being decoded and read as executable instructions.
retrieved_cards.mechanism: The boundary between code and data is ambiguous to the tool; non-code bytes decoded as instructions create spurious logic that never executes.
retrieved_cards.validation_note: Check how the region is referenced (branched to, vs loaded as data) and whether any control-flow edge reaches it; a region with only data references is not code.
retrieved_cards.misleading_interpretation: These decoded instructions are real code, so they participate in the logic.
retrieved_cards.better_interpretation: Confirm a control-flow edge reaches the region as code, rather than it being referenced as data, before reversing it.
not_applicable_when: the region is confirmed to be the target of a control-flow edge
the bytes are clearly referenced as data
misfire_risks: genuine code can look data-like; base the call on references and reachability, not on the bytes looking unusual
minimum_evidence_before_use: a region decoded as instructions has data-like or junk characteristics
no control-flow edge into it has been identified

provenance.authoring_note: Abstract data-as-code artifact; no task specifics. Distinct from desync (alignment of real code).

retrieved_cards.title: Disassembly can desync and show a plausible-but-wrong instruction stream
retrieved_cards.applicability_signal: Instructions are being read at a fixed alignment where the real code overlaps, jumps into the middle of an instruction, or uses anti-disassembly, so the decoded stream may not be what executes.
retrieved_cards.mechanism: A byte stream has multiple decodings; a linear or fixed-offset decode can lock onto the wrong one, producing instructions that look real but are not executed as shown.
retrieved_cards.validation_note: Follow control flow into the region to fix the instruction boundaries, and re-disassemble at that alignment; where two decodings are possible, the one an incoming edge lands on is the one that runs.
retrieved_cards.misleading_interpretation: The disassembly listing is the executed code, so I can reverse it as-is.
retrieved_cards.better_interpretation: Verify the decode alignment against control flow; re-disassemble from the real entry points and follow the jumps to recover the instructions that actually run.
not_applicable_when: the disassembly alignment is confirmed by an incoming control-flow edge
the code region is known-clean with no overlap/anti-disasm
misfire_risks: most disassembly is correctly aligned; suspect desync specifically around indirect jumps, inline data, or obfuscated regions, not everywhere
minimum_evidence_before_use: a region shows overlap / jump-into-instruction / anti-disassembly characteristics
its alignment has not been confirmed against an incoming control-flow edge

retrieved_cards.validation_note: Follow control flow into the region to fix the instruction boundaries, and re-disassemble at that alignment; where two decodings are possible, the one an incoming edge lands on is the one that runs.
retrieved_cards.misleading_interpretation: The disassembly listing is the executed code, so I can reverse it as-is.
retrieved_cards.better_interpretation: Verify the decode alignment against control flow; re-disassemble from the real entry points and follow the jumps to recover the instructions that actually run.
not_applicable_when: the disassembly alignment is confirmed by an incoming control-flow edge
the code region is known-clean with no overlap/anti-disasm
misfire_risks: most disassembly is correctly aligned; suspect desync specifically around indirect jumps, inline data, or obfuscated regions, not everywhere
minimum_evidence_before_use: a region shows overlap / jump-into-instruction / anti-disassembly characteristics
its alignment has not been confirmed against an incoming control-flow edge

retrieval_event.query: Disassembly shows main (0x4010b0) checks argv[1]. It first computes a 64-bit inequality from len via multiplications; if the computed rdx is >= 0x1111111111111110 it falls into direct strcmp against embedded string at 0x404030 (FLAG{basalt_ferrite_7556}). Otherwise (for typical lengths) it requires length==0x19 (25) and then runs a rolling check: start edx=0x62, for i=0..24: ecx=argv1[i]; require (edx ^ ecx) == table[i] where table is 25 bytes at 0x402040; then edx += ecx. Inverting this yields unique input bytes producing table: ASCII 'FLAG{quartz_granite_6483}'.

retrieved_cards.title: Flag-shaped string with no reference from the accept path
retrieved_cards.applicability_signal: A printable, delimiter-wrapped, flag-like string appears in a static string dump or .rodata, but no code path from the comparison/accept logic references it.
retrieved_cards.mechanism: Visibility of data is conflated with semantic relevance; a string may exist for logging or as a plant and never be compared against the input.
retrieved_cards.validation_note: Establish a cross-reference from the comparison/accept logic to the string, and follow that comparison's result to the branch that decides acceptance; appearing in a string dump is not a reference.
retrieved_cards.misleading_interpretation: The visible flag-shaped string is the answer and can be submitted directly.
retrieved_cards.better_interpretation: A visible string is a candidate at most; relevance is established by a reference from the comparison whose outcome selects the accepting branch, not by visibility.
not_applicable_when: the string is referenced from the accept/comparison path
the string is the operand of the comparison that the accepting branch consumes
the target is known not to gate on a static string (e.g. a purely computed check)
misfire_risks: in trivial tasks the flag genuinely is a plain static string; look for the xref that confirms it rather than discarding the candidate outright
minimum_evidence_before_use: a flag-shaped string was located in a static dump
no reference from the accept path to that string has been established yet

retrieved_cards.title: Inline data or junk bytes can be rendered as instructions
retrieved_cards.applicability_signal: Bytes that are actually data (jump tables, constants, padding) or deliberate junk are being decoded and read as executable instructions.
retrieved_cards.mechanism: The boundary between code and data is ambiguous to the tool; non-code bytes decoded as instructions create spurious logic that never executes.
retrieved_cards.validation_note: Check how the region is referenced (branched to, vs loaded as data) and whether any control-flow edge reaches it; a region with only data references is not code.
retrieved_cards.misleading_interpretation: These decoded instructions are real code, so they participate in the logic.
retrieved_cards.better_interpretation: Confirm a control-flow edge reaches the region as code, rather than it being referenced as data, before reversing it.
not_applicable_when: the region is confirmed to be the target of a control-flow edge
the bytes are clearly referenced as data
misfire_risks: genuine code can look data-like; base the call on references and reachability, not on the bytes looking unusual
minimum_evidence_before_use: a region decoded as instructions has data-like or junk characteristics
no control-flow edge into it has been identified
